newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan forces capture more ground from rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan forces capture more ground from rebels.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops driving into Tamil Tiger guerrilla territory in the north overcame heavy rebel resistance to capture an area near a fortified rebel-held junction town on Friday, the Defence Ministry said.
Ground troops estimated at least 25 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas were killed and more than 50 wounded in the day's fighting, it said in a statement.
The army lost one officer and eight soldiers in the battle while another officer and 11 soldiers were wounded, it said.
"Kfir aircraft and Mi-24 helicopters engaged targets in depth and provided close support," it said. "Terrorist reinforcements too were engaged by air causing heavy casualties."

Troops backed by tanks, artillery and air support resumed their advance at dawn towards the heavily fortified town of Puliyankulam, about 245 km (150 miles) north of the capital Colombo, in the mostly jungle-covered Wanni region, the ministry said.
The rebels retreated north of Puliyankulam, it said, adding the rebels had fired mortars at the soldiers.

Residents in Vavuniya, the gateway to the Wanni some 25 km (16 miles) to the south of Puliyankulam, reported hearing aircraft heading for the battlefield and the sound of artillery shells exploding in the distance throughout the day.
Casualties had poured into the town with ambulances and trucks carrying wounded racing through the streets, they said.

The troops had earlier captured the towns of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, and Nedunkeni, 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya, in an offensive codenamed Operation Jaya Sikuru, or Sure of Victory, that was launched from Vavuniya on May 13.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte told a news conference the aim of the offensive was to open a land supply route to Jaffna, 100 km (60 miles) further north, that would help rehabilitation work there.
The north-south highway has been closed for more than 10 years due to fighting between the rebels and government forces.
Ratwatte said troops had moved eight km (five miles) north of Omanthai, which army officials said was near Pandrikeithakulam village.

The LTTE, fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, accused the military in an overnight statement of systematically demolishing Tamil towns in the north.
"A concerted dismembering of Tamil society (town by town) is taking place, where Tamils' lifeline and self-sufficiency is progressively weakened by the Sinhala government," the LTTE statement said.

The rebels earlier said the military was firing artillery at heavily populated towns 32 km (20) miles from its forward defences, forcing civilians to abandon their homes and seek refuge in the jungle.
The military has denied their shells were aimed at civilians, saying they fired only at identified rebel targets.
The rebels also said Tamil property and food were looted by the armed forces at Nedunkeni. The Defence Ministry spokesman denied the charge.
Independent confirmation of the events was not possible as international media have not been allowed in the war zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began in 1983. The rebels say the toll is higher.
